utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a problem with the fact this is a photocopy, not the actual notebook. So, I mean, I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But there's no problem with the counsel to ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do apologise, but I had drawn the gentleman's attention to this, asking whether it was the same format. And I will reply again, yes, it's the same format.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the other platoon that you say was located, was that platoon located in the same area or in some other area? Was it the same town or the same hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was quite far away from us. It was not on the same hill, not on the same mountain. It was on another mountain, another location. I don't know if I can say that in open session, what the location was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So to the best of your understanding or the best of your knowledge, having looked at not just the front page but looked through this notebook, a copy of the notebook shown to you, it is your testimony under oath that this document is not generated by your platoon? You're absolutely 100 per cent positive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I can't say for sure on the basis of this copy. I can't say for sure that this was not generated by my unit, however, I do believe that it was not generated by my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether the other platoon that was doing similar work as you were doing, that was part of the same company and part of the same corps, used the same type of notebooks that your platoon was using?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I ask that I proceed into the substance, unless counsel wants to argue to the contrary that the gentleman is not qualified for me to point out the discrepancies in this particular intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the witness has just indicated he doesn't believe that this has come from his platoon. He certainly doesn't recognise it. He thinks that it came from somewhere else. How can he possibly now be asked questions in relation to the substance when he has no -- he had nothing to do with this particular notebook? In my submission, that would be improper and unfair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, your question is that this is your testimony under oath that this document is not generated by your platoon. You're absolutely 100 per cent positive? It's a very absolute question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So I believe that after the examination of those documents the witness gave a reasonable answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, that he could not -- the other side of the coin is that he cannot rule this out and being his -- he cannot say it is. He thinks it isn't. But he's not willing to rule out the possibility. Then when we look at the other facts, it is the same size, it is from a notebook that looked like all the other notebooks. Even if it were from another platoon, we can only assume that that platoon is using the same method of recording with the same sorts of devices, the same quality control or lack of control, sending it to the same areas. So I think, given that, one could reach a reasonable conclusion that this gentleman would be qualified to at least go on record to share with us the inconsistencies. Now, if the Prosecution -- because I get all these documents from them, if they can tell us exactly where these documents came from and whether they intend to produce a witness that we can question that witness regarding this intercept, then I will reserve that line of questioning for that witness. They would know. They have the originals. So they would be -- they should be able to produce the originals, show the gentleman the original. He might be able to have a better understanding. But at this point, I'm relying on what they gave us. And in this particular intercept, we see some glaring errors, glaring errors. And I'm not suggesting that this man wrote it down. Obviously, he doesn't recognise the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, are there any witnesses in the future to testify to this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, there will be, Your Honour. And yes it does happen to be a witness from a different platoon, which is what I was trying to indicate earlier and I know Mr. Karnavas did not want me to indicate that and just tried to get it through the witness. But I can tell you as a fact that there will be another witness from a different place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, you still have the opportunity in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, had I known this 15 minutes ago, I wouldn't have gone through that questioning. But with that representation, I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, very much. Ms. Sinatra, do you have any cross-examination or you prefer we have an early break?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I would prefer we have an early break. We need to make a physical transfer of podium, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What do you mean by physical?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I need to use the podium, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I could use the break as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will be prepared in 10 minutes to go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we will resume at 20 minutes to 6.00. Yes, we will resume at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just before I start my questioning, I'd like to bring to the Court's attention that we do have a Defence witness in the courtroom who is our expert witness, Mr. Ashkenasy. I believe it has already been ruled that expert witnesses have the right to listen to the testimony of the witnesses that have to do with their expertise. I would just like to let the Court know that Mr. Ashkenasy is in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What do you mean by in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Not in the courtroom. He's listening in the chambers outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. No objections to him sitting in the gallery.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you for the terminology.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. While I'm on my feet, I just wondered perhaps just as a matter of housekeeping I can go back to the issue that you asked me earlier relating to the disclosure of the tapes. I wanted to clarify one matter because I didn't want to seem misleading in any way whatsoever. I can indicate that we've provided all the relevant tapes to counsel and we have given access to counsel to the tapes that may not necessarily relate to the July 1995 period but that we do have in our possession. So they are aware of it. I understand that, in fact, Ms. Sinatra over the summer period did, in fact, come in and listen to a tape and/or she was also provided with some additional copies of tapes, which again we are not relating to conversations which we are not tendering. So the bottom line is, they are basically informed of what we do have in our possession and certainly have had access to everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just -- well, I guess I'm a little perplexed. First there were representations that they have nothing. Then she qualified by saying they gave us the relevant. Now it appears that aside from what they deem is relevant, they have other material. I would like a clear answer, perhaps they cannot give it to us today, but perhaps she could go back and meet with the senior trial lawyer and tell us exactly what tapes or reels they have. And because if that is the case, then I will be making a request for at least the Trial Chamber to review those and to see whether we should be entitled to any tapes that were not available. I know for a fact, that's why I was a little taken aback by the representation made earlier, I know for a fact that in the Krstic case there was one particular tape that was played or that they attempted to play and it became a very big issue. So -- and then she made this representation. So I would like to know exactly from the Prosecution what tapes they have. And I certainly don't want a Prosecutor determining what is relevant to my case, because they don't know what my case is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I hope that tomorrow morning if you are free you could meet with the Prosecution to discuss this matter in details. If there are any difficulties, just inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll do whatever we can to help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will meet with the Prosecutor, Your Honour. And I will -- certainly will do that and see whether we can resolve this amicably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to add my comments on the disclosure of the tapes. This is not -- this does not mean that it has to be relevant to the exact paragraphs in the indictment. We're challenging the reliability of the process of recording and taking the intercepts, and therefore, there are other areas that would be relevant to this issue besides just the specific information that they have outlined in the indictment. So we would like to have access to intercept information that -- especially in the Brdjanin case which I have just requested that we believe is very relevant to the process of intercepting conversations, transcribing them, and capturing them for -- in their archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My recommendation is that you join Mr. Karnavas in that meeting with the Prosecution tomorrow morning. We try to solve all those issues out of court. If there's still any problems, just don't hesitate to come to the attention of this Bench. Yes, Ms. Sinatra, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examined by Ms. Sinatra:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dobar dan, P-117. How are you this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm fine. And you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll well, thank you. I just want to go back on your direct testimony. I believe you laid a foundation that you were an amateur radio operator with the B and C license, which you acquired during your military service. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like to add the following: In addition to B also all the lower ranking permits and licenses that C, D, E, F included.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the highest ranking you have is B. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all ham operators all over the globe internationally take the same test that you did to become certified or licensed with B and C. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you were in the JNA starting in 1982. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you specialised -- I don't know how -- whether we need to go in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to be out of caution, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I would like to ask with the assistance of the usher to bring out P321. I don't know if we can put it on the ELMO. If we can, I would really appreciate the assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll try to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you take a look at what has been marked for identification purposes as P321 and you've seen this map before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, this map is a product of your unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You got this map from the command of my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just point on this map to -- I want you to point out several communications centres. And we will start with Konjuh. Could you show us where Konjuh is located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, the map would have to be on a larger scale for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's off the map. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it. I can't look around the edges of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Okresanica was located. Was it located on Mount -- I can't read it. I'm sorry. Majevica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Majevica. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, were Konjuh and Okresanica the centre of the BiH communications in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In 1995 they weren't -- the combination of the two did not comprise the centre of the communications for -- let's say for the 2nd Corps, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was included in the communications centre for the 2nd Corps, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, this has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm trying -- first of all, sir, you don't know what my purpose is in my questioning. I would like for you to identify since you do know the zone, the area, that you were ordered to monitor. It lies between three rivers, doesn't it? Can you just circle around the area that is your zone of monitoring from the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want to say -- as I'm to do it on this map, I can point out only part of this zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Because it is a gigantic zone, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You're quite right. It is gigantic and we have a part of the zone of responsibility here, a large part of the Drina Corps, and then there's the radio relay centre. But there's only a part of it on this map and some of the participants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I would like to go to the centre for the VRS communications system. Do you know where that was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radio relay station of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska was in Panorama located on a nearby hill overlooking Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Han Pijesak was the centre of VRS command at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The Main Staff. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the location of the communications centre, was it Mount Veliki Dzep; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that was its name. I can't point it out on the map right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The centre of all the vectors on this map, is that the VRS communications centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, this is the radio relay centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we're looking at the radio relay centre and I have the map out. Can you see the radio relay from what you have marked as Panorama? There's no direct link to Zvornik, is there? I think if you look at the top of your map --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it. I can't find the Palma participant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the top of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's no direct communication from Panorama to Zvornik, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has to go via a relay station about 30 or 40 kilometres away. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you through which relay centre, but of course yes, it had to go through one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you know that Zvornik is in a valley. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Surrounded by mountain peaks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's evident on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were in electronic warfare, are you familiar with where the location of the Croatian centre for communications was, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the IFOR communications centre was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a former member of the JNA, do you know where Bacenica is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, Madam. Tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Bacenica was the centre for the JNA of their electronic warfare. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You don't know where Kutlovo is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know that the signal coverage for all of Eastern Bosnia was very poor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean with radio relay apparatus or telephone signals or what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean intercepting radio waves on a site-to-site basis was very difficult in Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to move forward. Let's talk about in 1992 the Bosnian army when the war started called up all radio ham operators, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat your question, please. I really didn't hear it quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 when the JNA pulled all of its equipment out of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was a call for all amateur radio operators to come forward to set up electronic warfare units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing to do with that, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't called up in 1992 to help form an electronic warfare unit for the new BiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, you just mentioned a while ago that it was the JNA. I know that on the 20th of April, 1992, members of the JNA took me prisoner in a place near the town where I lived. And their goal was to capture ham radio operators. They came to look for radio stations and out of the four that had existed, they didn't find a single one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think the purpose of their taking you into custody was to make sure there were no amateur radio stations for the Bosnian Muslims or for the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose was, but I do know I was taken prisoner. At the same time, there was an announcement in the newspapers telling people to capture ham radio operators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were released and your equipment was not seized, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so, because they didn't find my equipment. I don't want to think about what might have happened had they found even a single radio station, because that's what they were looking for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to go into the political situation at the time, but I'd like to ask with the usher's permission -- I mean assistance, to show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D323. Sir, let me ask you if on during your direct examination you talked about having an RUP-12 ultra short wave radio that went from 30 to 70 megahertz. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this look like the piece of equipment you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it comes with a portable bag that goes with it as an amateur radio operator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but you mentioned two things that don't go together. What do you mean by amateur radio operator and a bag?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the kind of equipment that you had as an amateur radio operator, or is this the more sophisticated equipment that you gathered in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The equipment on the first picture on page 1 is an RUP-12, and it was only after the beginning of war operations that we were given this kind of equipment. As an amateur radio operator, I did not have this equipment, this kind of equipment before the outbreak of the war, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, this equipment that we're looking at, the RUP-12, was one of the more sophisticated pieces of equipment that you had at your communications centre, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had this equipment in 1982 when I was doing my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you used it in 1995 at Okresanica, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam. No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe on your direct testimony you testified that you used an RUP-12. You're saying you didn't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes, during the war, that's true. But in 1995 at Okresanica, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't testifying on -- the other day on the equipment you had at the communications centre in 1995, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995 we did not have an RUP-12. I know that for certain and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you go to the next picture. I believe that it's a -- this is like an amateur transceiver. Is this more like what you had used in the communications centre when you formed it in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, we did not have this type of equipment. I owned a piece of equipment of this kind, FT23R before the war. And it's 0.5 watts. The RUP-12 are 15 watts, well that is the beta above the accumulated -- the battery would not be able to take this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But all your equipment that you had at Okresanica, you didn't use batteries for it. You had it hooked up to an electric generator, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went through two generators in parallel, and we had two times 280 ampere hours which is 12 volts and 360 ampere hours because all our equipment would operate at 12 volts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your generators used gasoline, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you ran out of gasoline, the generators had to stop, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The generators, yes, that produced electrical power. But we also had 220 volt grid. And if that failed, then we had the generator. And there were batteries and the large corrector. So they could hold out for two days without any additional power generation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that in 1995 at the top of this mountain you had an electrical land line that provided you with electricity up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I would like to go on to the next piece of equipment that I have in front of you. It's an ICOM AH-7000. Would you look at the third page of that exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is the AH-7000 aerial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the antenna that you had at Okresanica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, all this information dates to 1992. How can this be valued for the year 1995? This is the antenna we had in 1992. And it was part of the equipment we had at that time. It was with this kind of antenna that we carried out part of our electronic activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying this is not the kind of antenna you had in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't need it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'd like to move on to other equipment. You have been talking about your UHER recorders.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the reason we're offering testimony here is so that the Trial Chamber can understand all this equipment better and so we can all have the correct picture of what circumstances existed at that time. The UHER recorder that you're talking about was a big reel-to-reel tape recorder, wasn't it, like we used in the 1960s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the tapes were those exposed tapes that went reel-to-reel. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can wind it, rewind it, tape over it all the time. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With that equipment, the quality of the tape itself diminished, each time you recorded over it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sometimes there was bleeding in of the previously recorded conversations into the ones you were trying to record at the moment, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were unimportant conversations. They would then be erased and then the tape would be rewound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you made the determination to re-use tapes because new tapes had not arrived, you didn't erase the tapes, did you? You recorded over them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you an example where one conversation could be taped over another if part of an unimportant conversation was recorded and then the tape was rewound. But we had a large number of tapes that we got from the radio station from a nearby town, and these were recorded at a speed quite a lot higher than the one we used. And then, there would be no possibility of an identifiable conversation appearing, because these were mainly tapes with music on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're stating that there was no distortion or pollution on the tapes that had been used over and over again that you recorded over that came from the radio station. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was. There was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go to another topic now. You know, you formerly work for the JNA, and -- because for me I still refer to the JNA -- I mean to the Serbian army as the JNA, will you tolerate my use of that term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We both know that we're talking about the army that was once the former Yugoslavia which became what is now the Serbian army. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 1995, the Serbian army had a lot more modern equipment than the BiH army did, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, while you were still with the JNA in the 1980s, a big modernisation of the equipment took place under the code name of Arios, A-r-i-o-s; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, Madam, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't aware of the code name for modernising all the equipment with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of it. I'm not familiar with that code name you've just mentioned, Arios.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe if I put it in its context a little clearer. This took place in the early 1980s. So you would have been 1982, and the process took place between 1982 and 1989 under this code name, Operation Arios.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You can answer any way you want to. I'm just trying to get, you know, the truth one way or the other. So thank you. If you don't know, I don't know is just fine. So you're not familiar with any of the components that were purchased during this Arios electronic warfare modernisation. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in the JNA 1982 until 1992. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Madam, no. I did my regular military service between 1982 and 1983. That was it. Afterwards, after I returned home in 1983, I was part of the reserve forces. And from 1985, I was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But you were still in electronic warfare. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a reserve officer, were you familiar with the Watkins Jenkins -- I'm sorry, Johnson WJ-8955 electronic system? I'm sorry that was Watkins Johnson.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it. But you keep referring to electronic warfare all the time. I was in electronic warfare, I this, I that. Madam, I was into electronic warfare during the war. It would be much more precise to say that I was into electronics, generally speaking, and that as a radio amateur I was into traffic, into communications using radio equipment. That would be the correct way to say it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when the JNA modernised and got all new equipment, they gave their old equipment to the VRS, didn't they? And the VRS is the Bosnian Serbian army -- Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of the special equipment that the JNA had was purchased by Bosnian Serb businessmen in the United States, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They also got new encryption machines for the JNA during this period, didn't they? Are you familiar with the encryption process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what I'm talking about when I talk about in-time processing of intercepted material?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must be talking about the description of material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within a certain period of time and not postponed before it's analysed. Let's say there's a 20-minute to two hour realtime, in-time processing of information.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, it wasn't always the same period of time. This very much depended on the quantity of material one had to deal with. All in all, you could say it was between 20 and 30 minutes, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But that's an intelligence, a signals term for doing the interception and communications with the authorities within a limited period of time. Are you familiar with that term, in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with something very much like it. I know that the length of time is supposed to be kept as short as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go back to the JNA. And there's a reason for this line of questioning. The JNA had 12 MiG-21 planes equipped with pods for surveillance under them, didn't they? MiG-21 is very modern, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, a very modern one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a surveillance plane, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know that that was indeed what it was used for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the JNA and the VRS shared information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such information, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that from the military situation you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only telling you what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you know that part of the intelligence operation, the communications operation, is also to send out misinformation or disinformation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're familiar with an operation from masking information called "Operativno Maskiranje"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term itself "Operativno Maskiranje," no, I'm not familiar with it. But I know that disinformation is spread to deceive the enemy. It's used by all armies of the world. Also by merely comparing intelligence gathered on the ground, you verify the truthfulness of a certain piece of information and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you stated, this is common in all military operations or intelligence operations throughout the globe, but it's also -- some of the terms used in this are misinformation, decoying, planting fake conversations, those are all part of it, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier about being familiar with the code names in the VRS and you went through a list and filed a list of what you considered were the code names that you were familiar with in your interception process. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I was familiar with those code names. Some were used on a number of different occasions. Some were used very often. It's difficult to say how many times each of those code names were used, but each of the code names was used on a number of different occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the code names that you talked about were code names for certain locations. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were also individuals that had code names, too, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide the Prosecution with a list of the code names of the individuals also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, Madam, you need to speak to someone from the command, because they were the ones forwarding materials, not me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't know the code name for Mr. Jokic, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the VRS had its own network of permanent interception stations at different locations, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I'll try to repeat this to see if I got it right. The VRS had several monitoring stations placed in different locations. Was that the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, they had a communications plan that was called code name V-a-t-r-a, "Vatra." Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name itself rings no bells. I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the interception devices used by the VRS, were they the RPK3s, Hungarian made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew they had special scanners, didn't you, the VRS, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what they had, except for the information that was available to us. Whenever we got information from them, that was all we had. But personally, I had no other knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I forgot whether you've answered -- forgotten whether you've answered this question or not. Did you tell me that you knew the VRS had more sophisticated equipment than the Bosnian army in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even back in 1992 they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's because they got most of their equipment from the JNA. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the war broke out in 1992, the main communication tower for the JNA had been the Stolice tower north of Tuzla. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said, Madam. One of the communications centres was there in Stolice. It was a radio relay centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of the communications from your unit went through -- you pronounce it Stolice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, you've just said that all our communications went through the radio relay centre at Stolice. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the BiH connection to all of Eastern Bosnia was through the Stolice tower. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could quite agree with you, Madam. Are you talking about the wartime period? Are you talking about peacetime? This is something we need to clarify before we go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about 1992 to 1995. It was a very important high area that was the connection for the BiH army to Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, this was very interesting for us. You're right, as far as that's concerned. But I think it's other people you should talk to about this, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your communications was basically greatly hindered and cut off by the VRS taking over this Stolice tower, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it really severed your connections with Croatia, Sarajevo, and Srebrenica, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea why you're asking me. I never worked in the area. I was not particularly familiar with the area. I don't see how I fit in with all of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because your specialty is communications and intelligence, and that's why I thought you must know your main connections to Sarajevo and Srebrenica were then cut off by the VRS taking over the Stolice tower. Maybe cut off is the wrong term, but severed and affected.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, I had no reason to think about these things, believe me. I had enough on my plate as it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) . It was only after that that a small unit was formed to intercept pilot's conversations at first. We monitored planes, aircraft, with great intensity, then afterwards we started monitoring combat on the front itself. That was what we reported about primarily. It was only in November or December that we had better equipment to be able to monitor communications that went through the radio relay centres. We could monitor part of their radio relay stations, the small ones, back in July or August, but the major communications we didn't begin monitoring before November or December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when they took over the tower, all you had basically were the ham operator equipment that you possessed personally. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't only hand-held equipment. There were stationary pieces being used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were all amateur radio enthusiasts that had been called up as part of the Territorial Defence, isn't that correct, under the Tito's Plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, will you please tell me which period you're referring to? Called up when? At which point in time? Can you please give me a date or a whole period of time and called up where. I have no idea what you're talking about, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know you do. We're just not communicating. When the war began in 1992, the effective organisations that you're talking about that were there to protect the public were part of a constitutional organisation called the Territorial Defence, and you worked with that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When -- you know, we lost the Stolice tower in 1992, but also the underground cables of communication for the BiH between Tuzla and Sarajevo and between Srebrenica and Sarajevo had been destroyed by the VRS, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way for me to be aware of that. I really had a lot on my plate at that point in time, to be quite honest. I was so busy. Believe me. That the communications themselves, I don't know. I suppose there was someone else to look after that. What I was doing was my job strictly, and that's how it worked. It worked as I've just described. You're talking about a different period, about the loss of Stolice and so on and so forth. There was a rupture in our communications and we wanted to put people back together, because people were scattered every where. You had no idea who was alive and who had been killed. Some people managed to escape. Sometimes you got word from certain people. And our aim was to make sure that all our equipment was in good working order, which it sometimes wasn't. We were facing lots of practical, technical problems. Those were our immediate tasks, to get the basic documents in order for establishing communication. I had to set up radio relay stations, which was my duty as a non-commissioned officer. This non-commissioned officer created by the JNA back in 1985. So I did my duty and my work was structured in this way, as I have just described to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to go back to my question which was whether you new that the underground cables for communications had been severed between Tuzla and Sarajevo and Tuzla and Srebrenica, which meant that all the telephone lines went from 1.080-something telephone lines to, like, 24 to the area. You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, believe me, I don't have this information. It's only now that I realise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- but you did know that there were no separate telephone lines designated for the Bosnian army versus the general public. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-117 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to start another topic. This might be a good place to quit for the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's almost 7.00. We will resume at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
